answer: Mass identity fraud is unattractive here not because it is always caught, but because it is never profitable to attempt at scale — the expected loss from slashing and rejection exceeds the expected gain. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a anchor as the anchor of the cost.
